paraJumbles.title: The school savings club

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Last year, the club used the interest earned on this account to buy fifty storybooks for the school library.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Every Monday, the children brought whatever coins they had saved and handed them to a teacher, who recorded each deposit in a register.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: More importantly, the children have learnt that small sums, saved regularly, can grow into something truly useful.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: Three years ago, a small school in a village near Nashik started a savings club for its students.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: At the end of each month, the teacher took the collected money to the nearest bank branch and deposited it in the club's account.

explanation: D opens: it introduces the savings club without referring back to anything.
B follows D: *the children* are the students of D, and B introduces *a teacher* who collects the coins.
E follows B: *the teacher* and *the collected money* both point back to B.
A follows E: *this account* is the club's bank account opened in E, and only a bank account earns interest.
C closes: *More importantly* ranks the lesson learnt above the first benefit (the books) in A.

paraJumbles.title: From queues to clicks

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: This changed when the railways launched an online booking system that allowed passengers to buy tickets from home or office.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Today, with an inexpensive smartphone in almost every pocket, most reserved tickets are booked online in a matter of minutes.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: For decades, buying a long-distance train ticket in India meant standing in a slow-moving queue at the station's reservation counter.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: At first, only people with a computer and an internet connection could use it, so the queues at stations barely shrank.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Passengers often had to take half a day off work for this, and even then a confirmed berth was not guaranteed.

explanation: C opens: it describes the old situation without referring back to anything.
E follows C: *for this* refers to standing in the queue described in C.
A follows E: *This changed* marks the turning point after the problem set out in C and E.
D follows A: *it* is the online booking system of A, and *At first* describes its early days.
B closes: *Today* completes the timeline — for decades, then the launch, at first, and today.

paraJumbles.title: Farm ponds

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: A subsidy covering most of the digging cost has changed their minds, and over four thousand ponds were dug in the region last year.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: In many dry districts of Maharashtra, farmers depend entirely on the monsoon, and a delay of even two weeks can ruin a season's crop.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Small farmers, however, were at first unwilling to give up even a corner of their land for a pond.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: To reduce this risk, many of them have begun digging farm ponds: shallow pits, lined with plastic sheets, that trap rainwater during heavy showers.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: This stored water keeps the crop alive during the dry spells that often follow, when the soil would otherwise crack and the plants wilt.

explanation: B opens: it states the problem (total dependence on the monsoon) without referring back to anything.
D follows B: *this risk* is the crop failure described in B, and *them* refers to the farmers.
E follows D: *This stored water* is the rainwater trapped by the ponds, and *the dry spells that often follow* come after the heavy showers of D.
C follows E: *however* and *at first unwilling* bring in the one drawback of the ponds after their benefit.
A closes: the subsidy *changed their minds* — the minds of the unwilling small farmers in C — and the four thousand new ponds round off the story.

paraJumbles.title: The tea stall goes digital

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: For most of that time, he accepted only cash, and on busy mornings he often ran out of change for customers carrying large notes.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: The effect was immediate: office-goers who used to walk past because they carried no cash began stopping for a cup.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Two years ago, his college-going nephew persuaded him to display a QR code so that customers could pay through UPI apps.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: His daily sales have nearly doubled since then, and he no longer keeps a tin of coins beside the stove.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Ramesh has been running a small tea stall near the bus stand in Mysuru for nearly twenty years.

explanation: E opens: it introduces Ramesh and his tea stall without referring back to anything.
A follows E: *that time* is the twenty years mentioned in E, and *he* is Ramesh.
C follows A: *Two years ago* marks the change from the cash-only years described in A.
B follows C: *The effect* is the effect of displaying the QR code, which let customers *who carried no cash* pay.
D closes: *since then* looks back to the change, and *no longer keeps a tin of coins* answers the problem of change raised in A.

paraJumbles.title: Tackling anaemia in schools

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: In districts where both steps have been followed for three years, the share of anaemic students has fallen by nearly a third.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: The good news is that the condition is easy and inexpensive to prevent, even in households with very little money.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Anaemia, a condition in which the blood carries too little oxygen, is one of the most common health problems among Indian teenagers.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: Without enough haemoglobin, a teenager tires easily, struggles to concentrate in class and falls ill more often than classmates who eat well.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Many schools now hand out a weekly iron tablet, and teachers talk to students about cheap iron-rich foods such as leafy greens, jaggery and pulses.

sentences.label: F
sentences.text: It usually results from a diet low in iron, the mineral the body needs to make haemoglobin.

explanation: C opens: it defines anaemia and introduces the topic without referring back to anything.
F follows C: *It* is anaemia, and F gives its cause, introducing the word *haemoglobin*.
D follows F: *Without enough haemoglobin* picks up the word just introduced in F and describes the harm.
B follows D: *The good news* turns from the harm described so far to prevention.
E gives the ways of preventing it promised in B; A closes: *both steps* are the iron tablets and the food lessons of E, and A reports the result.

paraJumbles.title: Guardians of the coast

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees that grow in the muddy strip where rivers meet the sea along India's coastline.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Mangroves also serve as nurseries for young fish and crabs, on which thousands of fishing families depend for a living.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Several coastal states are now replanting them, and satellite surveys show that the country's mangrove cover is slowly rising again.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: Their dense, tangled roots trap silt and break the force of incoming waves, shielding the villages that lie behind them.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Despite these benefits, large stretches of mangrove forest were cleared in past decades to make way for salt pans, fish farms and ports.

sentences.label: F
sentences.text: For this reason, coastal villages protected by thick mangrove belts have suffered far less damage in recent cyclones than exposed ones.

explanation: A opens: it defines mangroves without referring back to anything.
D follows A: *Their … roots* are the roots of the mangroves just defined.
F is fixed third and fits there: *For this reason* points back to the wave-breaking roots in D.
B follows F: *also* adds a second benefit (nurseries for fish) after the first (protection from waves).
E follows B: *Despite these benefits* sums up D, F and B before turning to the damage. C closes: *now replanting* answers the clearing described in E.

paraJumbles.title: Loans from a payment trail

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Without such documents, a lender had no reliable way to judge whether a borrower could repay, a gap that left many vendors at the mercy of moneylenders.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: The danger is that such loans will bypass the many vendors who still deal mostly in cash and so leave no digital trail.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: By studying these payment trails, some lenders now offer small loans that are repaid through tiny deductions from the vendor's daily receipts.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: For years, banks hesitated to lend to street vendors, who could show no salary slips, tax returns or any other proof of steady income.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Digital payments are quietly closing this gap, as every QR-code sale leaves a dated record of what a vendor earns each day.

explanation: D opens: it sets out the problem (no proof of income) and refers back to nothing.
A follows D: *such documents* are the salary slips and tax returns of D, and A sums the problem up as *a gap*.
E follows A: *this gap* can only point to the word *gap* in A; E cannot come earlier because no gap has been named before A.
C follows E: *these payment trails* are the daily records created by QR-code sales in E.
B closes: *such loans* are the small loans introduced in C, and *The danger is* adds the limitation that ends the paragraph.

paraJumbles.title: Self-help groups and credit

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Impressed by this record, banks began lending directly to the groups, treating their savings history as a substitute for collateral.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Yet researchers caution that credit is only a beginning, since without steady markets for their products, such businesses seldom grow.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: The pooled savings are lent to members in turn, usually for needs such as school fees, seeds or a sewing machine.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: This link with the formal banking system has allowed many members to start small businesses that they could never have financed alone.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: In many Indian villages, women have formed self-help groups of ten to twenty members who save small sums together every week.

sentences.label: F
sentences.text: Because this lending rests on trust and peer pressure, repayment rates in such groups are often higher than those of ordinary commercial borrowers.

explanation: E opens: it introduces self-help groups and refers back to nothing.
C follows E: *The pooled savings* are the small sums the members save together in E.
F follows C: *this lending* is the lending of pooled savings described in C, and F reports its result — high repayment.
A follows F: *this record* is the repayment record of F, which is why the banks started lending.
D follows A: *This link with the formal banking system* is the bank lending of A. B closes: *Yet* adds a caution, and *such businesses* are the ones started in D.

paraJumbles.title: The revival of block printing

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Over the last two decades, however, designers and online stores have built a new market among buyers willing to pay more for handmade cloth.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: This means the printer must press the same stretch of cloth up to a dozen times, letting each colour dry in between.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Hand block printing, in which carved wooden blocks are dipped in dye and pressed onto cloth, has been practised in parts of Rajasthan for centuries.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: As a result, younger members of these families are returning to the workshops, often pairing the old blocks with designs of their own.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Such slow, painstaking work could not compete when cheap screen-printed fabrics flooded the market, and many printing families abandoned the craft.

sentences.label: F
sentences.text: Every block is carved by hand, and a single design may need a dozen of them, one for each colour it contains.

explanation: C opens: it defines hand block printing and refers back to nothing.
F follows C: *Every block* refers to the carved blocks of C, and F adds that one design needs a dozen of them.
B follows F: *This means* draws the consequence of needing a dozen blocks — up to a dozen pressings of the same cloth.
E, fixed fourth, follows B: *Such slow, painstaking work* sums up the process in B.
A follows E: *however* turns from the decline to the revival. D closes: *As a result* follows from the new market in A, and *these families* are the printing families of E.

paraJumbles.title: Cold rooms at the farm gate

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Investors have been slow to build such a network because farmers rarely rent storage, and farmers rarely rent it because none exists nearby.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Their running costs, however, are negligible, and since space is rented by the crate, even a farmer with half an acre of tomatoes can use them.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Early trials suggest that farmers who hold back their produce for a week or two, instead of selling at harvest-time prices, earn about a quarter more.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: Every year, a large share of India's fruit and vegetables rots before reaching a consumer, even as city shoppers complain of high prices.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Small solar-powered cold rooms, though costly to install, offer a way out of this impasse because they can be placed at the edge of a village.

sentences.label: F
sentences.text: The culprit is not a shortage of produce but the lack of a cold chain, the network of refrigerated stores and vehicles that keeps harvests fresh.

explanation: D opens: it states the paradox (food rots while prices stay high) and refers back to nothing.
F follows D: *The culprit* names the cause of the waste in D and introduces the cold chain as a *network*.
A follows F: *such a network* can only be the cold chain of F; A describes a circular stand-off between investors and farmers.
E follows A: *this impasse* is the stand-off in A, and E admits that the cold rooms are *costly to install*.

B follows E: *Their running costs, however* contrasts with *costly to install*, and *Their* must refer to the cold rooms. C closes: farmers can *hold back their produce* only once the storage of E and B exists, and C gives the result.
